thread:
IncBot: 🔔 ALERT: latency spike + autoscale thrash detected on kv-service (prod-us-east). metric: kv_batch_queue_size / hpa_replicas oscillation.

Tilly O: I’m on pager, looking. any recent deploys?

Alex R: Maria rolled batching-window tweak at 08:12 (reduce window -> 50ms) to squeeze latency.

Maria V: yep, small change to continuous batching to reduce tail latency for chat workloads. rolled to canary then prod at 08:12. saw perf perf bump on our microbench but not full traffic.

Samir K: current symptoms: 5-10x 95p token latency for some frontends, KV cache size exploding on a subset of pods, HPA oscillating between 2 <-> 8 replicas every 60-90s.

Tilly O: Can you paste the most recent k8s metrics?

Samir K: logs/snippet:
```
# kubectl top pods -n inference | grep kv
kv-pool-5  1700m  12Gi
kv-pool-6  1900m  18Gi
# Prom: avg(kv_cache_entries) per pod jumped from 40k -> 1.2M in 3m
# HPA: replicas: 2 -> 8 -> 3 -> 7 over last 10min
```

Alex R: looks like batching window reduction increased request aggregation imbalance, building large KV caches due to more warmups + long-lived prefixes. warmup is fighting HPA: more replicas start, warm caches replicate, then cold start again when they scale down -> repeat.

Devex Ryan: @Maria V can we rollback that change until we stabilize?

Maria V: I can rollback but need a fix plan. If we revert, we might reintroduce the tail-latency we were trying to mitigate.

Ops Bot: Customer impact alert: 12 customers (tiered) with >5s median generation latency, 3 reporting 502 errors. Incident severity: SEV2.

Tilly O: Immediate mitigation options (prioritized):
1) increase HPA min replicas to reduce churn/hysteresis (quick k8s patch).
2) temporarily disable continuous-batching for kv-service (feature flag rollback).
3) patch batch window back to previous value.
4) throttle prefix warmups / reduce kv cache TTL.

Samir K: I’m applying (1) and (2) now:
```
kubectl patch hpa kv-service -n inference --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'
# feature flag: ffctl set kv.continuous_batching false --env prod
```

Samir K: patch applied. minReplicas=6 || feature flag disabled.

Tilly O: monitoring...

(3m later)

IncBot: metric update: hpa_replicas stabilized at 6, kv_cache_entries per pod shrank from 1.2M -> 120k, 95p latency dropping from 6s -> 1.4s.

Alex R: good signal. any customers still seeing errors?

Ops Bot: customer impact update: errors down to 1 customer with intermittent 502s; overall latency improving.

Maria V: I’ll queue a conservative rollback of the 50ms change to previous 80ms, but will do it behind a canary and traffic ramp. prefer not to fully revert yet — aim for a safer midpoint.

Devex Ryan: Also recommend we add a small HPA stabilization window and bump the scale-down stabilization seconds to avoid sawtooth. Suggest: spec.behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds=180

Tilly O: Good. Samir, can you add a temporary autoscaler hysteresis and increase grace period for kc warmup?

Samir K: doing both.
```
kubectl patch hpa kv-service -n inference --patch '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180}}}}'
# config change: kv.warmup.grace_ms = 60000 -> 180000
```

(10m later)

IncBot: telemetry snapshot: hpa stable 6 replicas, kv_cache_entries per pod ~90k, 95p gen latency ~900ms. No new 502s in last 5m.

Alex R: note: disabling continuous batching reduced aggregate throughput; we should watch token cost. Workload shape might need batching profiles per route.

Maria V: deployed canary patch rolling batch_window->80ms to 10% traffic. Monitoring memory and cache growth.

Devex Ryan: customer comms: I’ll draft a short note for affected customers: explain mitigation and ETA for full rollback/cfg.

Tilly O: Paging: I’ll keep this until metric stability for 30m then hand to next oncall. Action items now:
- Maria: finish safe canary roll and hold.
- Samir: keep autoscaler hysteresis in place for 2 hours then reassess.
- Alex: schedule follow-up to evaluate per-route batching.
- Devex Ryan: prepare customer note and postmortem stub.

Samir K: logging relevant PRs/deploys in incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/inc/INC-2111110000

(handoff)
Tilly O: handing off to Tilly O -> Next oncall: @Tilly O stays until 09:15 UTC, after that @Alex R picks up unless further escalation.

Alex R: ack, monitoring.

Tilly O: post-incident notes: probable root cause = aggressive batching window reduction combined with KV warmup behavior and too-aggressive HPA scale-down. Mitigations applied: raised min replicas, disabled continuous batching, introduced scale-down stabilization, reduced warmup replication panic. Follow-ups: revert permanent change until we have per-route profiles, add chaos tests for batching/warmup interaction, add alerting for abnormal kv_cache_entries growth.

Maria V: will open PRs for safer rollout process and add a canary gating job that simulates warmup.

IncBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED -> metrics stable for 25m. SEV2 -> downgraded to SEV3.

Tilly O: ending thread. I’ll own the postmortem doc draft.

Alex R: thanks team :thumbsup:
